titre_page: How do I connect the inputs and outputs of nodes? | Yop2D guide
description: In Yop2D an output takes only one wire, but an input can receive several: learn to connect nodes, including two paths leading to the same node.
h1: The inputs and outputs of nodes
carte: One output = one wire, one input = as many wires as you like.
etapes: The input is on the left, the outputs are on the right.
Pulling a new wire from an output replaces the old one.
Bring two outputs to the same input: two paths lead to the same node.
blocs: A node has **circles**: these are its inputs and outputs. The wires between them say in which order the nodes run. One simple rule to remember: **an output has only one wire, an input can have several.**

On the **left**, the input circle ({{lang:port_entrer}}): this is where the node receives the order to run. On the **right**, the output circles (for example {{lang:port_suivant}}): this is where the node hands over to the next one. Some nodes have several outputs, like a {{lang:noeud_condition}} with {{lang:port_vrai}} and {{lang:port_faux}}.
An output takes only one wire
If you pull a new wire from an output that is already connected, the new one **replaces** the old one. So an output can only lead to one place.
Pull a wire from a first output to the input circle of the node you want.
Pull a second wire from another output (or from another node) to the **same** input circle.
The first wire stays in place: the node runs as soon as one of these paths reaches it.

Example: a countdown has one output that fires every second and another when it is finished. Connect both to the same node that changes a text: the time shows in both cases, without building the node twice.

In the Blueprint **{ }** window, the script is written as text. When a node is reached by two paths, it is described only once; the other path ends with an arrow **↩**, which means “this node was already described above”.
To cut a wire, tap it. To redo it elsewhere, pull a new one from the output.
